perf.summary: Brent's improvement plus batched-GCD: the current Floyd cycle detection computes a 128-bit-ish ModMul GCD every single step; batching the product of |x-y| and taking gcd every ~128 steps cuts gcd calls by 100x.
perf.currentCost: Each iteration of the while loop calls Gcd (a full Euclid loop, ~O(log n) modulos) AND three F evaluations (each F is a ModMul = expensive 128-bit mul-mod). One gcd per step is the classic Pollard-Rho inefficiency.
perf.proposedChange: Accumulate the product `q = ModMul(q, AbsLong(x - y), n)` over a block of e.g. 128 steps, then call Gcd(q, n) once per block; on a hit, backtrack the block to isolate the real factor. Also adopt Brent's variant (single F per step using a saved x and power-of-two reset) to halve F evaluations vs Floyd's 3 F-calls per step.
perf.rationale: Reduces gcd invocations from one-per-step to one-per-128-steps (Euclid is the second-most-expensive op here), and Brent reduces ModMul calls per step from 3 to ~1.5. Standard, well-known 2-5x speedup for Pollard-Rho with identical factor output (modulo block backtracking).
perf.risk: Batched gcd can return n if a factor was absorbed by accumulation collision (product hits 0 mod n); must keep last block to retry step-by-step, and guard q against becoming 0. Brent changes the iteration order so the FIRST factor found may differ from Floyd's — but FindFactor only needs ANY nontrivial factor, and the public contract returns 'a factor', so observable top-level behavior (a valid divisor) is preserved, though the exact divisor for composite-with-3+-factors inputs may change. State this if exact-value determinism is required.

perf.summary: n%2 and n%3 trial checks can be a single combined check, and n&1 replaces n%2.
perf.currentCost: `n % 2 == 0` then `n % 3 == 0` are two modulos at entry of every Run call.
perf.proposedChange: Use `(n & 1) == 0` for the even test (mask vs divide). Keep n%3 (3 not power of two). Minor.
perf.rationale: n is the input; for n>=1 n&1 is identical to n%2==0 and is a 1-cycle AND vs a divide. Trivial but free.
perf.risk: n&1 equals n%2==0 only for non-negative n; Run is called on positive n to factor by contract, so safe. If negative n is ever passed, n%2 and n&1 differ for n<0 — but factoring negatives is undefined here anyway.

perf.summary: F does ModMul then +c then %mod; the final %mod can be a conditional subtract since ModMul already returns a value < mod and c < mod.
perf.currentCost: `(ModMul(x,x,mod) + c) % mod` — ModMul result is in [0,mod), c starts at 1 and grows in FindFactor. The trailing %mod is a full divide.
perf.proposedChange: If c is kept reduced (c < mod, which holds while c is small relative to n), then `long t = ModMul(x,x,mod) + c; return t >= mod ? t - mod : t;` replaces the divide with a branchless/conditional subtract. Add AggressiveInlining to F.
perf.rationale: ModMul output < mod and c < mod guarantee the sum < 2*mod, so a single conditional subtract suffices instead of a 64-bit modulo. Saves one divide per F call (called ~3x per Pollard step).
perf.risk: Requires c < mod; FindFactor increments c from 1 and rarely exceeds a few thousand, far below n for nontrivial inputs, but for tiny n the invariant c<mod can break — guard with c %= mod once in FindFactorWithC. Sum can overflow if mod near long.Max (2*mod overflow); Pollard targets fit since ModMul already constrains mod < 2^62 effectively. Note the overflow caveat.
